title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Morgan Lee
description: This PR tunes the continuous batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness across tenants and workloads, prevent starvation of low-priority/long-tail requests, and introduce configurable timeouts for queued requests. Motivation: under mixed workloads we observed multi-tenant unfairness and occasional starvation of low-throughput request classes (see ENG-8241). The previous scheduler favored throughput-optimal packing which increased P99 latency for smaller critical requests. Changes include: (1) adaptive queue buckets by size/priority; (2) age-based scheduling weight (aging) to prevent starvation while preserving throughput; (3) per-queue soft/hard enqueue timeouts and early-drop policies for overloaded nodes; (4) metrics/tracing and per-tenant fairness sliders exposed to the control plane; (5) unit and e2e perf tests and updated benchmarks. The description below contains a concise list of what changed and why, and links to follow-ups.

patch_summary: Refactor scheduler into policy-driven implementation; add age-based weights; implement per-queue timeouts and early-drop; expose fairness controls and metrics; add unit and perf tests; docs
review_comments: Aisha Patel: Overall approach LGTM. Two asks: 1) include a default that is conservative for Dedicated customers (they rely on throughput), 2) add a small microbenchmark showing impact on P99 for mixed workloads.

Author (Morgan Lee): Added a 'performance_profile' switch in scheduler_config.yaml with 'throughput_conservative' and 'fairness_balanced' presets. Also added perf_harness scenarios and results in docs/operational/scheduler-tuning.md.
Daniel Kim: Please clarify early-drop semantics and ensure we don't drop requests that can be retried safely; also add a metric for dropped_retries to help SRE investigate.

Author (Morgan Lee): Early-drop only triggers for queues exceeding soft_timeout AND when node OOM/pressure simulated signals are present; added dropped_retries counter and unit tests that validate retryable vs non-retryable semantics.
Sofia Ramirez: Request small nits: move magic constants to config and add comments explaining why 8 aging steps; otherwise approve after CI green.
Author (Morgan Lee): Moved constants to scheduler_config.yaml, added comments and a short note on the design tradeoff in the doc. Thanks!
ci_checks: benchmark-suite: pass (perf regression check: no regression on throughput; P99 improved in mixed workload scenarios)
benchmarks_summary: Mixed workload perf harness: baseline (old scheduler) vs tuned scheduler: 6-12% reduction in P99 tail latency for small low-throughput requests, negligible (<=1%) throughput impact for saturated GPU pools. Detailed numbers and harness config in docs/operational/scheduler-tuning.md.
known_issues: Under extremely bursty single-tenant workloads the fairness slider can slightly increase median latency; added guidance to docs on when to select throughput_conservative preset.
release_notes: Improved continuous batcher scheduler: configurable queueing fairness, starvation prevention via aging weights, enqueue timeouts and early-drop policies; exposes metrics and tuning presets. Recommended: start with 'fairness_balanced' for multi-tenant clusters and 'throughput_conservative' for Dedicated GPU pools.
